content.overview: The final specialist product is not just an answer; it is a defensible record that another qualified reviewer can reconstruct, challenge and continue. Confidence must be proportional to evidence, and unresolved risk must remain visible.

vocabulary.definition: A calibrated description of how strongly the available evidence supports the working conclusion.
Important questions not resolved by the available evidence.
Structured explanation of the evidence, reasoning, controls, alternatives and limitations supporting a recommendation.

sections.title: Show the reasoning chain
sections.body: Link the recommendation to observations, discriminating evidence, test results and the evidence that weakened alternatives. Avoid presenting the final answer as obvious or inevitable.

sections.title: Calibrate confidence
sections.body: Use language such as possible, probable, strongly supported or confirmed only when the evidence justifies it under the facility's defined terminology. A specialist should be able to say what would change the conclusion.

sections.title: Handoff the open work
sections.body: Written plus verbal transfer should include current status, active holds/controls, evidence, pending tests, deadlines, residual risk and the next responsible role, with opportunity for cross-checking.

workedExamples: A case can end with 'probable root-zone oxygen stress with unresolved secondary pathogen contribution' if that wording better matches the evidence than a falsely certain single diagnosis.
commonMistakes: Hiding uncertainty to sound more expert.
Giving the conclusion without the evidence trail.
Omitting pending tests and active controls from handoff.
content.practicalApplication: Present a five-minute case defense and a one-page handoff: evidence, differential, discriminating findings, response, confidence, residual risk and next action.
content.summary: Professional diagnostic work is transparent enough to be audited, challenged and safely continued by another qualified person.
